messages:
alex: ran a cpu-side perf + FlameGraph focused on the token pipeline after the batching heuristic tweak. seeing a recurring hotspot: PyObject_Call -> Token.__init__ -> tokenizer._bytes_to_tokens, and lots of futex_waits in the kernel stacks

maria: can you paste the perf command and the top collapsed stacks? want to know if its GIL or our scheduler mutex causing the churn

alex: perf commands i ran: 
```
perf record -F 400 -g --call-graph dwarf -a -- sleep 60
perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
./flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg
```
trimmed top stacks from out.folded (humanized):
- PyEval_EvalFrameEx; PyObject_Call; Token.__init__; tokenizer._bytes_to_tokens; _PyBytes_Resize; futex_wait
- batcher::push_and_maybe_flush; batcher::flush_locked; std::mutex::lock; futex_wait
- kv_cache::lookup; kvstore::maybe_load; pread; fsync

sam: interesting. the token path being in Python while holding batcher lock would explain high futex/syscall ratio

jane: did you run `perf sched` or `perf top` to observe context-switch density?

alex: yes `perf sched record -o sched.data sleep 30` then `perf sched latency` showed lots of short wait periods and many wakeups per request. `perf top` during a hotspot window flagged PyObject_Call and PyThread_acquire_lock.

maria: reminds me of the change where we serialised incoming bytes into Token objects inside the critical section. before we had a C++ fast-path that parsed bytes without allocating Python objects.

alex: exactly. the new aggressive-batching heuristic causes many small batches where we convert buffers to Token objects under the same lock the scheduler uses to coordinate batches. result: GIL-ish behavior + kernel futex churn.

perf-bot: perf summary: total samples: 120k; PyObject_Call 34%, tokenizer._bytes_to_tokens 20%, PyThread_acquire_lock 14%, futex_wait 9%

sam: quick experiments to isolate root cause:
1) `PYTHONMALLOC=malloc` run to see allocations effect
2) `py-spy record -o pyspy.svg -- python -m module_under_test` to capture Python stacks without intrusive ptrace artifacts
3) run with `-X faulthandler` and `gc.disable()` to check GC spikes

alex: did 1+2: py-spy shows a ton of Token.__init__ frames and small python-level parsing frames. when I disabled allocations (`PYTHONMALLOC=malloc`), overhead didn't disappear, so not pure allocator contention.

maria: hypothesis: lock scope + python object creation while holding the lock leads to short critical sections but many of them -> syscall and futex thrash. plus if kv_cache eviction triggers, file I/O can amplify blocking.

sam: mitigation options:
- move tokenization off the locked path: copy raw slices while holding the lock, do bytes->Token conversion after unlock
- reintroduce C++ fast-path for common short tokens/bpe cases to avoid PyObject overhead
- tweak batching heuristic to avoid sub-threshold tiny batches (e.g., don't flush until N tokens or T ms)
- add per-thread object pools for Token to reduce allocation pressure

alex: i prototyped the first option: change flush path to copy buffer references into a local vector under lock, then release lock and convert to Token objects. perf run after patch: PyThread_acquire_lock samples dropped from 14% to 4%, futex_wait down ~30%.

maria: any impact on latency tail? p50/p99 numbers?

alex: p50 flat (~6.2ms), p99 improved ~15-20% on synthetic load. CPU cycles per request down ~10%.
jane: nice. please also run longer 5-10 minute perf sessions to capture rare kv_cache eviction interactions. those can show up as fs read spikes in perf maps and distort totals.

devops: when you push the canary, please collect artifacts: `perf.data`, `out.folded`, `flame.svg`, and `perf sched` outputs to /mnt/artifacts/perf/token-pipeline/ so we can compare runs. add `--profile=cpu` on canary job.

sam: operational follow-ups:
- add a unit/regression test asserting the batcher never holds the lock during Python object construction (can be a sanitizer/assert in debug builds)
- tune batching heuristic: prefer slightly larger windows for small seq-lens to amortize conversion cost
- add telemetry for batch-size distribution and time-inside-lock histogram to monitor in prod

maria: also try a run where kernel-selection routes small sequences to the fast C++ path explicitly, while routing complex transforms to Python path. this gives us deterministic coverage and isolates the perf cliff.

alex: will include in PR: patch to reduce lock-scope + perf command README + attached flame.svg and pyspy.svg. i'll also run the long 10m perf and attach results.

jane: once PR lands we'll stage it, roll canary, and watch p99 + syscall rates. if stable, promote to canary and then prod.

perf-bot: note: remember to include nsys traces if you run mixed CPU/GPU instances — kernel-selection may fallback to CPU for some seq-lens and that changes the hotspot mix significantly.

alex: good point. for mixed boxes i'll capture `nsys profile --output nsight.qdrep --sample=cpu,os:1000` and correlate with perf.

maria: :thumbsup: thanks. this was a clean root cause and a low-risk fix.
